title: The pretraining corpus of an in-context tabular model: invented tables from random priors (data only)
request: Collect and store everything a future model needs, never train: for 26.6b, the many invented tables a TabPFN-style model is pretrained on.
spec: dclab_core/priors.py: three priors (a random structural causal model, random shallow trees, a noisy linear model), categories, missing cells, uneven classes and noise columns, one table per seed; dclab_rnd/lake/priors.py writes them to the lake in shards with a split per seed and a learnability check; make priors.
plan: Generate, never train: the run is the owner's GPU.
Make every table reproducible from its seed, so the corpus is its seeds.
Split by the seed's hash so a sealed part exists before any model sees the corpus.
Check each table carries signal, and keep the ones that do not, marked, as the prior holds them.

decisions.decision: Category codes are permuted, not ranks of the underlying value.
decisions.why: Ranks would give an ordinal meaning a real category does not have, and a model would learn a shortcut.

decisions.decision: The outcome of the causal model is never a root node.
decisions.why: A root has no causes among the nodes, so the shown features could only be its effects or noise; a prior should hold causes too.

decisions.decision: A seed already in the corpus is never written again, whatever the start or the shard size; a seed in two shards is an error.
decisions.why: Shard names alone could not prevent duplicates across overlapping runs, and repeated tables would inflate the training stream and the manifest.

change: dclab_core/priors.py, dclab_rnd/lake/priors.py, the lake command priors, make priors, tests/test_lake_priors.py, the plan's status.

findings.defect: The learnability check ran very slowly while the gate ran.
findings.scenario: Thirty tables did not finish in five minutes at a load average above 200.
findings.cause: The gradient-boosting check starts one thread per core for every table, competing with the gate's processes.
findings.fix: make priors and the test run the check on one thread (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1).

findings.defect: Overlapping runs or another shard size added duplicate tables, and the manifest counted them.
findings.scenario: build(20, 0, 5) then build(20, 10, 5) gave 39 tables for 30 seeds.
findings.cause: Shard names depend on where chunks start; the manifest counted lines.
findings.fix: build skips seeds already kept; the manifest refuses a seed in two shards.

findings.defect: learnable called tables it never checked tables without signal.
findings.scenario: Seed 570 with class counts [2, 14, 2, 0, 49]: majority 1.0, no signal; about 2.9% of 2,000 seeds.
findings.cause: An empty class code counted as a class of zero rows.
findings.fix: Empty codes are dropped; a class of one row returns signal None, counted apart in the manifest.

findings.defect: A causal-model table did not say which shown features are the outcome's effects.
findings.scenario: An effect with identity activation and low noise is a near copy of the outcome; a corpus could not be filtered for it.
findings.fix: params.effects_shown lists their positions in the shown table; the manifest counts such tables.

measurements.name: The first corpus
measurements.gate: a description, not a gate: most tables should carry a signal a quick model finds (more than half above 2 points of lift)
measurements.result: 2,000 tables (seeds 0 to 1,999), 693,617 rows, 36 MB: 1,402 train, 314 dev, 284 sealed; 651 causal, 654 trees, 695 linear; a quick model beats the majority class by more than 2 points on 1,342 of the 1,954 checkable tables (mean lift 0.096; causal 489 of 641, trees 409 of 634, linear 444 of 679); 46 not checkable; 351 tables show an effect of the outcome.
measurements.against_gate: 1,342 of 1,954 is above half; the description holds.
measurements.next: The pretraining run is the owner's (GPU); then 26.6's sealed set of 30 real datasets.
limits: Lift over the majority class says a table carries a signal, not that the prior resembles real tables.
A quick model's lift on the held-out rows of a small table is noisy.

outcome: A reproducible corpus of invented tables with its sealed part, in the lake; the model itself is the owner's run.
lessons: A corpus that is its seeds can be checked, regrown and split before anything learns from it.
risks: Priors are a guess about what real tables look like; a model pretrained on them is evidence about the priors until it is measured on 26.6's sealed real datasets.
